case.label: B
case.text: Interface endpoints for every available service would also cover CloudWatch Logs, Secrets Manager, SSM and other services the tasks may need at run time, and the stem does not say which services the tasks call, so a cautious architect could argue that the broad set avoids a later failure. The case fails because the stem says the security team reviews every resource added to the VPC and asks for least operational overhead, so a blanket set of endpoints is the opposite of what is asked, and A already covers the stated need (private image pull).

case.label: D
case.text: A candidate could argue that scaling the service in further (lower minimum task count) leaves instances empty and that the Auto Scaling group then shrinks, so no capacity provider is needed. The case fails because service auto scaling changes only the task count and never the instance count; instances are removed only when the capacity provider managed scaling lowers the group size, which needs target capacity 100 percent and tasks packed onto fewer instances (binpack). Minor gaps: the stem does not mention managed termination protection, and a placement strategy affects only newly placed tasks, but neither opens a second answer set.
